# Screen catalog — planr dashboard (SPEC-016)

The dashboard design was produced by `/planr-pipeline:design` over three review
rounds and is signed off in
[`design/design-spec.md`](../../.planr/specs/SPEC-016-dashboard/design/design-spec.md).
All 27 mockup artboards are in
[`.planr/specs/SPEC-016-dashboard/design/mockups/`](../../.planr/specs/SPEC-016-dashboard/design/mockups/)
at three frame sizes: Desktop (1440×1024), Tablet (834×1194), Mobile (390×844).

This catalog maps each design-spec §9 screen entry to its implementing source
file(s) and notes any fidelity drift between spec and build.

---

## Shell chrome (all screens)

**Design-spec reference.** §3 Spacing & Layout, §4 Components Inventory, §5 Navigation.

**Source files.** `lib/dashboard/app/shell.js`, `lib/dashboard/app/ds.css`.

The shell renders:

- A **264px left rail** — workspace switcher, view nav (Overview · Graph · Board · List · Sprints · Activity), Filters section (Status dropdown + Type checkboxes: Epic / Feature / Story / Task / Spec), and a "Live — watching .planr/" indicator with a pulse ring animation.
- A **56px sticky top bar** — hamburger (mobile), breadcrumb, ⌘K search field, "Agile + Spec" mode chip, live badge, theme toggle (light default / `.dark`), export button, notifications bell.

**Fidelity.** Matches spec exactly. The design-spec §3 lists tablet reflow at
≥768px (icon-only rail, search bar hidden) and mobile at <768px (rail collapses
to hamburger, compact top bar). `ds.css` implements these via container queries.
QA confirmed all rail elements and top-bar elements are present in `shell.js`.

## Screen 1 — Overview

**Mockups.** [`01-overview-desktop.png`](../../.planr/specs/SPEC-016-dashboard/design/mockups/01-overview-desktop.png) · [`01-overview-tablet.png`](../../.planr/specs/SPEC-016-dashboard/design/mockups/01-overview-tablet.png) · [`01-overview-mobile.png`](../../.planr/specs/SPEC-016-dashboard/design/mockups/01-overview-mobile.png)

**Source file.** `lib/dashboard/app/views/overview.js`

**What it shows.** Four KPI tiles (total artifacts, done %, blocked count,
in-progress count), a segmented status bar, a specs table with per-spec progress
indicators, and a mini activity feed. All data is bound to `GET /api/graph`.

**Acceptance criterion.** KPI counts must match `/planr-pipeline:status` for the
same project. This is guaranteed structurally: both surfaces use the same
`classifyStatus` rules and, when the CLI is available, the same CLI output.

**Fidelity.** Matches spec §9 Screen #1. Zero off-palette hex literals in the
view module (QA-verified). US-003 AC6 (KPI parity with `/status`) is met by
design via the shared graph engine.

## Screen 2 — Graph

**Mockups.** [`02-graph-desktop.png`](../../.planr/specs/SPEC-016-dashboard/design/mockups/02-graph-desktop.png) · [`02-graph-tablet.png`](../../.planr/specs/SPEC-016-dashboard/design/mockups/02-graph-tablet.png) · [`02-graph-mobile.png`](../../.planr/specs/SPEC-016-dashboard/design/mockups/02-graph-mobile.png)

**Source file.** `lib/dashboard/app/views/graph.js` (904 lines), layout engine at `lib/dashboard/app/vendor/graph-layout.js`

**What it shows.** A layered directed acyclic graph of project artifacts. Nodes
render as `ds-node` cards with a type-coloured left accent, id, title, and status
badge. `contains` edges are solid muted SVG paths; `depends_on` edges are dashed
primary SVG paths. Blocked nodes and all nodes transitively dependent on them are
highlighted in the warning colour. A legend, minimap, zoom controls, pan-by-drag,
an Agile/Spec mode toggle, and a right-rail inspector (shown on node select) are
all present.

**Layout.** The `graph-layout.js` vendor module implements a four-stage pipeline:
filter by model (agile or spec), rank nodes into tiers, order within tiers using
a median heuristic, then place into absolute pixel coordinates on a 4-point grid.
It has zero external dependencies.

**Fidelity.** Matches spec §9 Screen #2 and all US-006 ACs. Zero hex literals in
the view module.

**Design-spec open question: mobile graph.** The design-spec §10 notes that the
mobile graph ("shrunken nodes + hidden minimap") remains a zoomed-out overview
and that "a real mobile graph needs a different representation (e.g. a collapsible
list/tree)." The build implements the zoomed-out mobile layout per the approved
mockup; a collapsible tree representation is deferred.

## Screen 3 — Board

**Mockups.** [`03-board-desktop.png`](../../.planr/specs/SPEC-016-dashboard/design/mockups/03-board-desktop.png) · [`03-board-tablet.png`](../../.planr/specs/SPEC-016-dashboard/design/mockups/03-board-tablet.png) · [`03-board-mobile.png`](../../.planr/specs/SPEC-016-dashboard/design/mockups/03-board-mobile.png)

**Source file.** `lib/dashboard/app/views/board.js`

**What it shows.** Four status columns (Outstanding · In Progress · Blocked · Done)
with count badges. Each artifact is a `ds-cardlet` with a type-accent strip, id,
title, and a status footer. A "Group by" toolbar lets users regroup cards by
status, sprint, or feature. The groupBy logic (`groupBy(nodes, key)`) is exported
from the same file; sprint grouping is keyed by `sprintId`, feature grouping by
`featureId`. The board is read-only: no drag-to-move, no `contenteditable`
(confirmed by QA grep).

**Fidelity.** Matches spec §9 Screen #3 and US-007 ACs. Zero off-palette hex.

## Screen 4 — List

**Mockups.** [`04-list-desktop.png`](../../.planr/specs/SPEC-016-dashboard/design/mockups/04-list-desktop.png) · [`04-list-tablet.png`](../../.planr/specs/SPEC-016-dashboard/design/mockups/04-list-tablet.png) · [`04-list-mobile.png`](../../.planr/specs/SPEC-016-dashboard/design/mockups/04-list-mobile.png)

**Source file.** `lib/dashboard/app/views/list.js`

**What it shows.** A dense artifact table with a type-chip filter toolbar (Epic /
Feature / Story / Task / Spec) and sortable columns: id, title, type, status,
updated. The header row is sticky. Filtering and sorting are client-side — no
server round-trip. Filter updates propagate via the `planr:filter-change` custom
event from `filterState` in `main.js`.

**Fidelity.** Matches spec §9 Screen #4. US-007 AC4 (client-side filter) is met.
Mobile: table scrolls horizontally inside its card (per design-spec §3 reflow
note — the table does not squish on narrow screens).

## Screen 5 — Detail

**Mockups.** [`05-detail-desktop.png`](../../.planr/specs/SPEC-016-dashboard/design/mockups/05-detail-desktop.png) · [`05-detail-tablet.png`](../../.planr/specs/SPEC-016-dashboard/design/mockups/05-detail-tablet.png) · [`05-detail-mobile.png`](../../.planr/specs/SPEC-016-dashboard/design/mockups/05-detail-mobile.png)

**Source files.** `lib/dashboard/app/views/detail.js`; data assembly via `assembleDetail(node)` exported from the same file.

**What it shows.** A drill-down view reached at `#detail/:id`. Header: type badge,
id, title, status badge. Meta grid: created, updated, agent, parent ids (specId /
storyId / featureId). Acceptance criteria rows: parsed from `## Acceptance
Criteria` lines in the markdown body. Subtask checklist: parsed from `- [ ]` and
`- [x]` items in the body, rendered read-only. `dependsOn` chips: each chip is a
link (`<a class="dep-chip" href="#detail/${depId}">`) for in-app navigation.
Ship/QA reference links: rendered when present in frontmatter.

**The design-spec mentions a Gherkin section.** US-008 AC2 specifies "Gherkin
acceptance criteria rows (rendered from the matching `-gherkin.feature` file if
present)." The implementation parses criteria from the artifact's own body
(`## Acceptance Criteria` section) rather than loading the separate
`-gherkin.feature` file. The QA report confirms the acceptance-criteria parse
works; the separate gherkin file is not loaded at runtime. This is a partial
match: the spirit of the AC is met (criteria are shown) but the source is the
body, not the `.feature` file.

**Fidelity.** Partially matches spec for Gherkin sourcing (see above). All other
Detail ACs match.

## Screen 6 — Sprint

**Mockups.** [`06-sprint-desktop.png`](../../.planr/specs/SPEC-016-dashboard/design/mockups/06-sprint-desktop.png) · [`06-sprint-tablet.png`](../../.planr/specs/SPEC-016-dashboard/design/mockups/06-sprint-tablet.png) · [`06-sprint-mobile.png`](../../.planr/specs/SPEC-016-dashboard/design/mockups/06-sprint-mobile.png)

**Source files.** `lib/dashboard/app/views/sprint.js`; burndown data via `getSprintData(graph)` exported from the same file.

**What it shows.** Sprint KPI tiles: committed count, completed count, carryover
count, velocity. A burndown SVG with an actual line (`<polyline
class="burndown-actual">`), a shaded area fill (`<path
class="burndown-area">`), and a dashed ideal line (`<polyline
class="burndown-ideal">`). A by-assignee table with done / in-progress / blocked
counts per team member. There is no charting library: the SVG is constructed
directly. `getSprintData` identifies the active sprint (type `sprint`, status not
`done`), collects task nodes by `sprintId`, and computes metrics and burndown
points from `updatedAt` timestamps.

**Fidelity.** Matches spec §9 Screen #6 and US-008 ACs. Zero hex literals in the
view module. No charting library imports (QA-confirmed).

## Screen 7 — Activity

**Mockups.** [`07-activity-desktop.png`](../../.planr/specs/SPEC-016-dashboard/design/mockups/07-activity-desktop.png) · [`07-activity-tablet.png`](../../.planr/specs/SPEC-016-dashboard/design/mockups/07-activity-tablet.png) · [`07-activity-mobile.png`](../../.planr/specs/SPEC-016-dashboard/design/mockups/07-activity-mobile.png)

**Source files.** `lib/dashboard/app/views/activity.js`; event parsing via `parseActivityEvent(rawData)` exported from the same file.

**What it shows.** A live-streaming feed of `.planr/` change events. The view
opens `EventSource('/api/events')` on mount and closes it via `unmount()`. Each
SSE message is prepended to the feed as an entry with: a status dot, a change
description, an actor/timestamp, and a relative time label. While connecting, a
"Connecting…" placeholder is shown. A `planr:activity-event` custom event is
dispatched on `document` on each entry so the shell's live badge can pulse.

**Fidelity.** Matches spec §9 Screen #7 and US-008 ACs. Zero hex literals.

## Screen 8 — Search (⌘K)

**Mockups.** [`08-search-desktop.png`](../../.planr/specs/SPEC-016-dashboard/design/mockups/08-search-desktop.png) · [`08-search-tablet.png`](../../.planr/specs/SPEC-016-dashboard/design/mockups/08-search-tablet.png) · [`08-search-mobile.png`](../../.planr/specs/SPEC-016-dashboard/design/mockups/08-search-mobile.png)

**Source file.** `lib/dashboard/app/views/search.js`

**What it shows.** A command-palette overlay (scrim + auto-focused input + result
list). Activated by ⌘K / Ctrl+K from anywhere in the app via `cmdkDispatcher` in
`main.js`, or by clicking the ⌘K field in the top bar. Typing performs a fuzzy
match using a character-trigram index over artifact ids and titles. Results update
as the user types (max 20). Keyboard navigation: ↑/↓ moves the cursor, Enter
navigates to `#detail/<id>`, Escape closes the overlay.

**Fidelity.** Matches spec §9 Screen #8 and US-007 ACs. Zero hex literals.

## Screen 9 — Empty state

**Mockups.** [`09-empty-desktop.png`](../../.planr/specs/SPEC-016-dashboard/design/mockups/09-empty-desktop.png) · [`09-empty-tablet.png`](../../.planr/specs/SPEC-016-dashboard/design/mockups/09-empty-tablet.png) · [`09-empty-mobile.png`](../../.planr/specs/SPEC-016-dashboard/design/mockups/09-empty-mobile.png)

**Source file.** `lib/dashboard/app/empty-state.js`

**What it shows.** Rendered by `overview.js` when `GET /api/graph` returns
`{ nodes: [], edges: [] }`. Displays: the planr mark, a short explanatory
message, a command chip showing `/planr-pipeline:plan`, and a CTA button. The
spec (FR5, "honest empty/large states") requires "never a blank screen" and "one
next action." The implementation shows exactly one action.

**Fidelity.** Matches spec §9 Screen #9. An empty `.planr/` yields an empty graph
without error (QA confirmed: `graph-reader.mjs` returns `{ nodes: [], edges: [] }`
when the directory is absent or empty).
